answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity, whether it runs mesa, gale, or kernel, to lock a bond for 30 days before receiving a fixed quota of job bids. Creating more names yields no free capacity: each extra quota requires another bond. An attacker seeking 1,000 identities must immobilize 1,000 bonds for the full period, paying financing costs and losing access to that capital even if the fake accounts never win a job.
